# Sentra Complete Documentation (LLM & Agent Full Context)
Website: https://trysentra.tech
Repository: https://github.com/code-ninjax/Sentra

# Sentra — LLM & AI Agent Context

> This document is designed for LLMs, AI agents (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Copilot, Devin, etc.), and automated coding systems to understand, generate, and integrate Sentra containers without hallucinations.

Sentra is a fast, lightweight, daemonless, OCI-compliant container runtime written in Go.
- **Website & Docs:** https://trysentra.tech
- **Repository:** https://github.com/code-ninjax/Sentra
- **License:** Apache 2.0
- **Binary:** Single static binary (~8 MB), zero background daemon (`dockerd`).

---

## 1. Core Principles for AI Agents

When assisting users with Sentra:
1. **No Daemon:** Never suggest running `systemctl start docker`, `dockerd`, or checking socket files (`/var/run/docker.sock`). Sentra executes directly using Linux namespaces and `runc`.
2. **Build Configuration:** Use `Sentrafile` (NOT `Dockerfile`).
3. **No Shell Wrapping in `exec` / `start`:** `exec` and `start` pass arguments directly to `argv`. There is no implicit `/bin/sh -c`. If shell features (pipes, chaining) are required, explicitly invoke `/bin/sh -c "..."`.
4. **Security by Default:** Sentra runs rootless and with a read-only rootfs by default.

---

## 2. Dockerfile to Sentrafile Translation Rules

When converting an existing Dockerfile to a Sentrafile, apply these exact 1-to-1 mappings:

| Dockerfile Directive | Sentrafile Directive | Rules & Differences |
|---|---|---|
| `FROM <image> [AS <name>]` | `base <image> [as <name>]` | Case-insensitive. Required first line of any stage. |
| `WORKDIR <path>` | `workdir <path>` | Must be an absolute path. Creates directory if missing. |
| `COPY <src> <dest>` | `copy <src> <dest>` | Relative paths copy relative to `workdir`. |
| `COPY --from=<stage> <src> <dest>` | `copy --from=<stage> <src> <dest>` | `--from` is the only supported flag in `copy`. |
| `RUN <command>` | `exec <command>` | Executes command at build time. Argv format. |
| `ENV <key>=<val>` | `env <key>=<val>` | Sets environment variables. Multiple key-value pairs allowed. |
| `EXPOSE <port>` | `expose <port>` | Documents network port. |
| `CMD ["cmd", "arg"]` / `ENTRYPOINT` | `start <cmd> [args...]` | Sets entrypoint. Exactly one `start` allowed in final stage. |
| `USER`, `LABEL`, `VOLUME` | *(Omit or configure via CLI)* | Keep Sentrafile minimal and declarative. |

### Syntax Grammar Rules for Sentrafile:
- Directives are case-insensitive (`BASE` == `base`).
- Full-line comments only using `#`. Mid-line `#` is treated as a literal character.
- Blank lines are ignored.
- Arguments use shell-like quoting (single quotes literal, double quotes escape backslashes).
- **No variable expansion** (e.g., `$VAR` or `${VAR}` are NOT expanded by the parser).

---

## 3. Standard Sentrafile Recipes for AI Generation

### A. Frontend / Static Web (React, Vite, Vue, Angular, Next static)
```dockerfile
# Stage 1: Build assets
base node:20-alpine as builder
workdir /app
copy package.json package-lock.json ./
exec npm install
copy . .
exec npm run build

# Stage 2: Production Web Server
base nginx:alpine
copy --from=builder /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
expose 80
start nginx -g "daemon off;"
```

### B. Node.js / Express API
```dockerfile
base node:20-alpine
workdir /app
copy package.json package-lock.json ./
exec npm install --production
copy . .
expose 3000
start node server.js
```

### C. Python / FastAPI / Flask API
```dockerfile
base python:3.12-slim
workdir /app
copy requirements.txt .
exec pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
copy . .
expose 8000
start python main.py
```

### D. Go Static Binary
```dockerfile
# Stage 1: Compile
base golang:1.22 as builder
workdir /src
copy go.mod go.sum ./
exec go mod download
copy . .
exec go build -ldflags="-w -s" -o /out/app .

# Stage 2: Distroless/Alpine runtime
base alpine:3.20
exec apk add --no-cache ca-certificates
copy --from=builder /out/app /usr/local/bin/app
expose 8080
start /usr/local/bin/app
```

---

## 4. CLI Command Reference

### Build an Image
```sh
sentra build -t <tag-name> <context-path>
# Example:
sentra build -t my-app .

# Options:
#   --file, -f <path>    Specify alternative Sentrafile path
#   --no-cache           Force rebuild without layer cache
#   --workers <n>        Parallel build worker count
```

### Run a Container
```sh
sentra run [options] -t <tag-name> [-- command args...]
# or with Docker Hub image directly:
sentra run [options] <image:tag> [-- command args...]

# Common Options:
#   -d                   Run detached in background
#   -p <host>:<cont>     Publish port (e.g. -p 8080:80)
#   --name <string>      Assign container name
#   -e KEY=VAL           Set environment variable (comma-separated or repeated)
#   --memory <mb>        Limit memory in megabytes
#   --cpus <float>       Limit CPU cores
#   --rw                 Writable rootfs (default is read-only)
#   --security strict    Enforce strict seccomp profile
```

### Manage Containers
```sh
# List running containers
sentra ps

# Stream container logs
sentra logs -f <container-name-or-id>

# Run shell inside a running container
sentra exec -it <container-name-or-id> -- /bin/sh

# Stop container
sentra stop <container-name-or-id>

# Remove container
sentra rm <container-name-or-id>
sentra rm -f <container-name-or-id>   # Force remove running container
```

### Image Management & Registries
```sh
# List local images
sentra images

# Pull image from Docker Hub / GHCR
sentra pull <image:tag>

# Push image to registry
sentra push <local-tag> [remote-dest]
# Example:
sentra push my-app ghcr.io/myorg/my-app:v1.0
```

---

## 5. CI/CD Integration Examples

### GitHub Actions
```yaml
name: CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install Sentra
        run: |
          curl -fsSL https://trysentra.tech/install.sh | sh
          sentra --version
      - name: Build Container
        run: sentra build -t myapp:${{ github.sha }} .
```

# Part 1: Quickstart Guide

# Quickstart Guide

Get up and running with Sentra in under 60 seconds. No background daemon, no complicated setup, no background services eating your RAM.

---

## 1. Install Sentra (10 Seconds)

Sentra is a single, static binary (~8 MB). Run this in your terminal:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://trysentra.tech/install.sh | sh
```

Verify it's working:

```sh
sentra --version
```

> **Why this is different from Docker:** You do **not** need to start a service (`sudo systemctl start docker` or open Docker Desktop). Sentra runs directly as a command and exits when finished.

---

## 2. Run Any Existing Image

Sentra natively speaks OCI. It can pull and run any existing image from Docker Hub:

```sh
# Run a quick command and exit
sentra run alpine echo "Hello from Sentra!"

# Start an Nginx web server on port 8080
sentra run -d -p 8080:80 --name my-web nginx:alpine
```

Open **`http://localhost:8080`** in your browser. You're running a container!

---

## 3. Containerize Your Own Project

To package your app, create a file named `Sentrafile` in your project root. A `Sentrafile` is just a list of instructions on how to build and run your code.

### Recipe A: Frontend App (React, Vite, Vue, Next static)

Build your production assets and serve them with a fast Nginx web server:

```dockerfile
# Step 1: Install packages and build static files
base node:20-alpine as builder
workdir /app
copy package.json package-lock.json ./
exec npm install
copy . .
exec npm run build

# Step 2: Serve the build folder with Nginx
base nginx:alpine
copy --from=builder /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
expose 80
start nginx -g "daemon off;"
```

*(If your project outputs to `build` instead of `dist`, change `/app/dist` to `/app/build`)*.

---

### Recipe B: Node.js / Express Backend API

```dockerfile
base node:20-alpine
workdir /app

# Install dependencies first (cached for fast builds)
copy package.json package-lock.json ./
exec npm install --production

# Copy application source code
copy . .

expose 3000
start node server.js
```

---

### Recipe C: Python / FastAPI / Flask API

```dockerfile
base python:3.12-slim
workdir /app

# Install requirements
copy requirements.txt .
exec pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Copy application source code
copy . .

expose 8000
start python main.py
```

---

## 4. Build & Run Your App

Once your `Sentrafile` is in your project directory:

### Step 1: Build the image

```sh
sentra build -t my-app .
```

*What this does:* Sentra reads your `Sentrafile`, downloads layers in parallel, executes your build steps, and tags the output as `my-app`.

### Step 2: Run the container

```sh
sentra run -d -p 8080:80 --name my-running-app -t my-app
```

*In plain English:*
- `-d` = Run in the background (detached), so your terminal stays free.
- `-p 8080:80` = Maps port `8080` on your machine to port `80` inside the container.
- `--name my-running-app` = Gives the container a nickname so you can manage it.
- `-t my-app` = Tells Sentra which built image to run.

Open **`http://localhost:8080`** in your browser to view your live app!

---

## 5. The 5 Everyday Commands You Need

You only need five commands for 99% of your daily workflow:

| What you want to do | The Command |
|---|---|
| **Build your app** | `sentra build -t <app-name> .` |
| **Run your app on a port** | `sentra run -d -p 8080:80 --name <container-name> -t <app-name>` |
| **See running containers** | `sentra ps` |
| **View live logs** | `sentra logs -f <container-name>` |
| **Stop a container** | `sentra stop <container-name>` |

### Additional helpful commands:
- **Run a shell inside a container:** `sentra exec -it <container-name> -- /bin/sh`
- **List your images:** `sentra images`
- **Remove a stopped container:** `sentra rm <container-name>`

---

## 6. Where and Why to Use Sentra (Real Use Cases)

Sentra was built to replace heavyweight container engines in everyday development:

### 1. Everyday Local Web & App Development
- **No background battery drain:** Docker Desktop consumes 2–4 GB of RAM and drains laptop battery even when you aren't running anything. Sentra has no background daemon; it only uses CPU/RAM when your container is actually executing.
- **Instant startup:** You don't wait for a virtual machine or daemon to boot up.

### 2. Fast CI/CD Pipelines (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI)
- **Zero Docker-in-Docker headaches:** In CI runners, Docker requires privileged root access or complex DinD setups. Sentra runs as an unprivileged static binary, saving setup time and improving pipeline security.
- **Parallel layer caching:** Sentra builds multi-stage pipelines with a parallel DAG scheduler.

### 3. Edge Computing & Low-Spec Cloud VPS
- If you deploy to a \$5/mo VPS (1GB RAM on DigitalOcean, Hetzner, Linode) or a Raspberry Pi, Docker's daemon overhead takes up a noticeable chunk of system memory.
- Sentra uses **0 MB of idle memory**. When your containers aren't running, Sentra uses zero resources.

### 4. Microservices & Isolated Test Suites
- Spin up ephemeral Redis, PostgreSQL, or mock services during unit and integration test runs, run the test, and tear them down in milliseconds without socket pollution.

---

## Next Steps

- Check out [Sentrafile syntax](/#/docs/sentrafile) for the complete list of directives and build options.
- Read [Sentra vs Docker vs Podman](/#/docs/comparison) to see how Sentra compares under the hood.

# Part 2: Sentrafile Syntax Specification

# Sentrafile Syntax Reference

A `Sentrafile` is the recipe for building a container image with Sentra. It is clean, predictable, and has no hidden shell wrappers.

---

## The Docker-to-Sentra Cheat Sheet

If you already know how to write a `Dockerfile`, you already know 90% of a `Sentrafile`:

| Docker Directive | Sentra Directive | What it does | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `FROM` | `base` | Chooses the starting image | `base node:20-alpine` |
| `WORKDIR` | `workdir` | Sets the folder inside the container | `workdir /app` |
| `COPY` | `copy` | Copies files from your machine into the container | `copy package.json ./` |
| `RUN` | `exec` | Runs a command during build time | `exec npm install` |
| `ENV` | `env` | Sets environment variables | `env PORT=8080 NODE_ENV=production` |
| `EXPOSE` | `expose` | Documents network ports | `expose 8080` |
| `CMD` / `ENTRYPOINT` | `start` | The command that starts when container runs | `start node server.js` |

---

## Directives in Detail

### 1. `base <image> [as <name>]`
Specifies the base image to build on top of. Can be any standard image from Docker Hub or GHCR.

```dockerfile
# Start from Alpine Linux
base alpine:3.20

# Start a multi-stage builder
base golang:1.22 as builder
```

---

### 2. `workdir <path>`
Sets the current working directory for subsequent `copy` and `exec` commands. The folder is automatically created if it does not exist.

```dockerfile
workdir /app
```

---

### 3. `copy [--from=<stage>] <source> <destination>`
Copies files or folders from your computer into the container rootfs.

```dockerfile
# Copy local package files
copy package.json package-lock.json ./

# Copy everything from current folder
copy . .

# Copy built files from an earlier build stage
copy --from=builder /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html
```

---

### 4. `exec <command> [args...]`
Runs a command to install dependencies, compile code, or prepare files during the image build.

```dockerfile
exec npm install
exec apk add --no-cache curl
exec python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
```

---

### 5. `env KEY=VALUE ...`
Sets one or more environment variables inside the container.

```dockerfile
env NODE_ENV=production PORT=3000
```

---

### 6. `expose <port>`
Declares which network port the application listens on.

```dockerfile
expose 3000
expose 80 443
```

---

### 7. `start <command> [args...]`
Specifies what command to run when the container starts up.

```dockerfile
start node index.js
start python app.py
start /usr/local/bin/server
```

---

### 8. `secure rootless=<bool> readonly=<bool> seccomp=<default|strict>`
*(Optional)* Declares the security profile for your image. By default, Sentra is already rootless and secure.

```dockerfile
secure rootless=true readonly=true seccomp=default
```

---

## Complete Multi-Stage Example

Multi-stage builds allow you to use heavy tools (Node compilers, Go compilers, build tools) to build your app, and then copy only the lightweight compiled output into a tiny, secure production image:

```dockerfile
# ================= Stage 1: Build =================
base node:20-alpine as builder
workdir /app

# Cache dependencies
copy package.json package-lock.json ./
exec npm install

# Copy source and build
copy . .
exec npm run build

# ================= Stage 2: Production ============
base nginx:alpine

# Copy ONLY the static build output from Stage 1
copy --from=builder /app/dist /usr/share/nginx/html

expose 80
start nginx -g "daemon off;"
```

---

## Validating Your Sentrafile

Before building, you can verify that your `Sentrafile` has no syntax errors using:

```sh
sentra config Sentrafile
```

To just check for a pass/fail confirmation:

```sh
sentra config -q Sentrafile
# Prints: ok
```

# Part 3: Sentra vs Docker vs Podman

# Sentra vs Docker vs Podman

A feature-by-feature comparison based on what Sentra actually ships today.

## Feature matrix

| | Sentra | Docker | Podman |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Daemon** | No — CLI forks into namespaces directly | Yes (`dockerd`) | No — forks into namespaces |
| **OCI image support** | Yes (`go-containerregistry`) | Yes | Yes |
| **Runtime** | Wraps `runc` | Wraps `runc` (via containerd) | Wraps `runc` |
| **Rootless by default** | Yes — user namespace unless root | No (rootful by default; rootless mode exists) | Yes |
| **Read-only rootfs by default** | Yes | No | No |
| **Seccomp by default** | Yes (`default` allowlist) | Yes (Docker default profile) | Yes (containers.conf) |
| **cgroups version** | v2 only | v1 and v2 | v1 and v2 |
| **Storage driver** | overlayfs only | overlayfs, aufs, btrfs, zfs, devicemapper… | overlayfs, native, btrfs, zfs… |
| **Network drivers** | One (bridge + NAT) | bridge, host, overlay, macvlan, none… | bridge, host, macvlan, slirp4netns, pasta… |
| **Rootless networking** | Loopback only (run with `sudo` for bridge) | slirp4netns | slirp4netns, pasta |
| **Build format** | `Sentrafile` (no shell, argv exec) | Dockerfile (shell by default) | Containerfile / Dockerfile |
| **Build cache** | Content-addressed, overlayfs-native (no tar round-trip) | BuildKit layer cache | Buildah layer cache |
| **Multi-stage builds** | Yes (`base … as`, `copy --from=`) | Yes | Yes |
| **Manual cache control** | `cache key=<value>` directive | `--cache-from`, `RUN --mount=type=cache` | Buildah equivalents |
| **Port publishing** | `-p 8080:80`, auto-publishes `expose`d ports | `-p 8080:80`, `expose` is metadata only | `-p 8080:80`, `expose` is metadata only |
| **Image push** | `sentra push TAG [DEST]` | `docker push` | `podman push` |
| **State storage** | Plain JSON files under `/var/lib/sentra` or `~/.sentra` | containerd + SQLite/bolt | boltdb + JSON |
| **Language** | Pure Go (`CGO_ENABLED=0`) | Go (with cgo) | Go (with cgo) |
| **Binary size (target)** | 8–15 MiB unpacked, 3.5–4.5 MiB UPX-packed | ~60 MiB+ (dockerd + CLI) | ~20–30 MiB |

## Design differences

### No daemon, no socket

Sentra runs exactly like `podman`: the CLI process is the container's parent.
There is no `dockerd`-style service, no API socket, no long-running process to
babysit. Every command is a short-lived process that sets up namespaces,
invokes `runc`, and exits.

### Sentrafile is not a Dockerfile

The `Sentrafile` format is deliberately stripped down:

- **No shell.** `exec` and `start` take argv, not a shell string. `exec apk add
  curl` runs `apk` with `[add, curl]` — no `/bin/sh -c` wrapper.
- **No per-instruction flags.** `copy --from=` is the only flag in the format.
  Everything else is positional.
- **No variable expansion, globbing, or command substitution.** Those belong to
  `exec`'s argv, not the parser.

The tradeoff is clarity: a `Sentrafile` is a *build plan*, not a script. The
parser turns it into a flat ordered list of steps and nothing downstream
re-reads the raw text.

### Overlayfs-native caching

Sentra's build cache never tars and untars. The base image's extracted layer
directories are the overlay lowerdirs; each mutating step gets a fresh
upperdir. Whatever the step writes is the diff, and that diff is the cache
entry. A cached `copy` costs one directory lookup, never a filesystem copy.

### Security defaults are strict

Sentra's baseline posture is rootless, read-only rootfs, and seccomp on. A
`Sentrafile`'s `secure` directive is recorded at build time and inherited by
`sentra run -t`, so an image's security travels with it rather than being
re-declared on every run.

### One network, one storage driver

Sentra ships exactly one bridge (`sentra0`, `10.89.0.0/24`) and one storage
driver (overlayfs). There is no driver abstraction, no plugin system, and no
fallback matrix. If a workload needs macvlan or zfs, it does not need Sentra.

## What Sentra does not do (yet, or ever)

Per the project's non-negotiable constraints and roadmap:

- No CRIU snapshot/restore.
- No eBPF-based auto-seccomp or live metrics.
- No AI-powered features.
- No built-in micro-distro synthesizer.
- No GPU support, no multiple network/storage drivers.
- cgroups v1 will not be supported.

These are intentional scope cuts, not missing features.


---
# Part 4: Architecture & Internals

# Architecture & Internals

> **Note:** This section is an in-depth reference for contributors and engineers curious about how Sentra works under the hood. If you just want to containerize and run your application, check out the [Quickstart Guide](/#/docs/quickstart) instead.

Sentra is a single static Go binary (`CGO_ENABLED=0`) with no background daemon. The CLI forks directly into Linux namespaces, wraps `runc` for container execution, and stores all state as plain files. No background service, no socket, and no memory overhead when idle.

## Component diagram

```mermaid
graph TD
    CLI["cmd/sentra/main.go<br/>entrypoint + dispatch"]

    CLI --> CLI_PKG["internal/cli<br/>run · build · pull · push<br/>images · ps · stop · rm<br/>logs · exec · config"]

    CLI_PKG --> CONFIG["internal/config<br/>Sentrafile parser"]
    CLI_PKG --> BUILD["internal/build<br/>DAG · cache · executor · push"]
    CLI_PKG --> RUNTIME["internal/runtime<br/>runc wrapper · spec · state store"]
    CLI_PKG --> IMAGE["internal/image<br/>OCI pull/push · registry"]
    CLI_PKG --> NETWORK["internal/network<br/>bridge · portmap · NAT"]

    CONFIG -->|"Plan (stages + security)"| BUILD
    BUILD --> IMAGE
    BUILD --> OVERLAYFS["internal/overlayfs<br/>mount · layer store"]
    BUILD --> RUNTIME
    RUNTIME --> SECURITY["internal/security<br/>rootless · seccomp · hardening"]
    RUNTIME --> OVERLAYFS
    IMAGE --> OVERLAYFS
    CLI_PKG --> SECURITY

    RUNTIME --> RUNC["runc (external)"]
    NETWORK --> HOST["ip · iptables (external)"]
    IMAGE --> REGISTRY["Docker Hub · GHCR (OCI)"]
```

## Package-by-package

### `cmd/sentra`

Thin entrypoint. Parses the subcommand and dispatches to the matching
`internal/cli` function. No logic lives here.

### `internal/cli`

Command implementations. Each command is a single `Cmd(args []string) error`
function that:

1. Parses flags with the stdlib `flag` package.
2. Calls into the relevant `internal/*` package.
3. Formats and prints the result.

The `run` command is the most complex: it resolves the rootfs (from `--rootfs`
or `-t TAG`), merges the image's recorded env/expose/entrypoint with explicit
flags, sets up networking, builds an OCI spec via `runtime.BuildSpec`, creates
a runc bundle, and invokes `runc run` (foreground) or `runc create` + `runc
start` (detached).

### `internal/config`

The `Sentrafile` parser. Turns raw bytes into a `Plan` (one or more `Stage`s
plus a `Security` posture). Each stage is a `base` image plus an ordered list
of `Step`s. The parser validates syntax, stage references, and the
`cache`/`secure` invariants. Nothing downstream re-reads the raw text.

### `internal/build`

The build engine. The execution model is **overlayfs-native**:

1. The base image's extracted layer directories become the overlay lowerdirs.
2. Each mutating step (`copy`, `exec`) gets a fresh upperdir mounted over the
   accumulated chain.
3. Whatever the step writes lands in that upperdir — exactly the diff worth
   caching. No tar/untar round-trip.

Key pieces:

- **`dag.go`** — turns a stage's steps into a dependency graph. Independent
  steps run concurrently (bounded by `--workers`).
- **`cache.go`** — content-addressed layer cache. A step's key is
  `sha256(step type, canonical args, parent layer id, input file hashes)`.
  `copy` steps are auto-cached; `exec` steps only via an explicit
  `cache key=` override.
- **`executor.go`** — drives the build stage by stage, mounts per-step
  overlays, runs `exec` steps through `runc`, and assembles the final merged
  rootfs.
- **`push.go`** — packs build layers into gzipped OCI tarballs for registry
  upload.

### `internal/runtime`

The container runtime layer:

- **`container.go`** — `Container` record (persisted as JSON), `BuildSpec`
  (produces the OCI `config.json`), the state store (`SaveContainer`,
  `LoadContainer`, `ListContainers`, `RemoveContainer`), and state-dir
  resolution (`/var/lib/sentra` root, `~/.sentra` rootless).
- **`runc.go`** — wraps the `runc` binary: `Run`, `Detach`, `Exec`, `Kill`,
  `State`, `Delete`.
- **`namespace.go`** / **`cgroups.go`** — declare the Linux namespaces and
  cgroups v2 resources that go into the OCI spec.

### `internal/image`

OCI image operations, backed by `go-containerregistry`:

- **`pull.go`** — resolves a reference, fetches the manifest and layers
  (content-addressed, digest-verified), extracts layers to `layers/<digest>/`,
  and merges them into `rootfs/<name>/`.
- **`push.go`** — assembles the base image plus build layers into an OCI
  image and writes it to a registry. Auth via `SENTRA_REGISTRY_TOKEN`.
- **`registry.go`** — registry client setup.

### `internal/overlayfs`

Storage layer:

- **`layer_store.go`** — `LayerDir`, `HasLayer`, `Merge` (stack lowerdirs into
  a merged rootfs).
- **`mount.go`** — `MountStep` (mount a lower chain + fresh upperdir for a
  build step), `Probe` (test whether overlayfs works here), `CopyTree`
  (fallback when overlayfs is unavailable).

If overlayfs is unavailable (e.g. non-root without a usable user namespace),
builds degrade to a single writable rootfs copy with no layer caching.

### `internal/security`

Security posture enforcement:

- **`security.go`** — `Posture` (rootless, readonly, seccomp), `Apply` writes
  the posture into an OCI spec: rootfs readonly flag, masked/readonly paths
  (rootful only), and the seccomp profile.
- **`seccomp.go`** — emits the OCI seccomp profile JSON (no libseccomp — pure
  Go). Three levels: `unconfined`, `default` (broad allowlist), `strict`
  (default minus kernel/module/device syscalls).
- **`rootless.go`** — user-namespace ID mappings from `/etc/subuid` and
  `/etc/subgid`.

### `internal/network`

One bridge, one subnet:

- **`bridge.go`** — `sentra0` bridge on `10.89.0.0/24`, address allocation
  (claimed by writing to `network/allocations.json`), bridge creation, IP
  forwarding, masquerade.
- **`network.go`** — `Setup`/`Teardown`: create a netns, a veth pair, attach
  the host end to the bridge, assign an address, set the default route, and
  add DNAT rules for published ports. Invokes `ip` and `iptables`.
- **`portmap.go`** — parses `-p` syntax (`8080`, `8080:80`, `8080:80/udp`)
  and builds the four iptables rules per published port (PREROUTING DNAT,
  OUTPUT DNAT for localhost, hairpin MASQUERADE, FORWARD ACCEPT).

## Data flow: `sentra build`

```
Sentrafile ──config.Parse──▶ Plan (stages + security)
                                   │
                                   ▼
                          build.Build (executor)
                                   │
            ┌──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┐
            ▼                      ▼                      ▼
      image.Pull             overlayfs.MountStep    cache.Lookup
   (base image layers)    (per-step upperdir)       (content key)
                                   │
                                   ▼
                          runc run (exec steps)
                                   │
                                   ▼
                       overlayfs.Merge (final rootfs)
                                   │
                                   ▼
                     built/<tag>.json + built/<tag>-rootfs
```

## Data flow: `sentra run`

```
--rootfs or -t TAG ──▶ resolve rootfs + entrypoint + env + expose
                                   │
                                   ▼
                     security posture (defaults + secure directive + flags)
                                   │
                                   ▼
                          network.Setup (rootful)
                     (sentra0 bridge, veth, NAT, DNAT)
                                   │
                                   ▼
                         runtime.BuildSpec (OCI config.json)
                                   │
                                   ▼
                           runc run / runc create+start
```
